title: Pete Warden on local AI, open models, voice interfaces, the future of hardware
lede: In a Data Exchange interview, Moonshine co-creator Pete Warden argues local models are already good enough for most work and are held back mainly by usability and a lack of marketing.

points: Warden says big AI companies have little reason to promote local models because they are hard to monetize.
A 9B-parameter model needs about 9 GB at 8 bits, and Q4 quantization squeezes it onto a 4 GB graphics card.
Machines with large unified memory, such as a 256 GB M5 Studio, can run models with hundreds of billions of parameters.
He argues local models should become an operating system service for apps, a direction he sees Apple heading.
Commercial guardrails can block benign work such as white-hat security research, another reason to run models yourself.

points.text: Commenters with home rigs describe using open models for serious systems work, from compiler bugs to kernel hardening.
One local-AI fan concedes the economics favor data centers, where batching keeps hardware far better utilized.
Others doubt ordinary users will spend thousands on hardware when most never self-hosted far simpler software.
Nvidia is blamed for neglecting consumer GPUs, which commenters say keeps stronger local models out of reach.
